# M-Dash Killer

A Claude Code plugin that removes the em dash character (U+2014) from every file Claude writes, then tells Claude which lines changed so it can fix the punctuation properly.

## Problem

Instructing Claude not to use em dashes via prompts or CLAUDE.md does not work reliably. The model forgets the rule often enough that the character keeps appearing in generated files.

## Solution

A PostToolUse hook that runs after every Write, Edit, or MultiEdit call. It scans the file on disk, replaces U+2014 with a spaced short hyphen, and returns a message naming every changed line. Claude is then required to re-read each sentence and apply the correct punctuation.

## Optional terminal guard

A PreToolUse hook on Bash commands catches em dashes in shell arguments (commit messages, PR bodies). Off by default. Can be set to block the command or rewrite it automatically.

## What it does not cover

- Claude's chat replies (conversation text, not files)
- Files above 5 MB
- Non-UTF-8 files

## Install

/plugin marketplace add compota334/Em-Dash-Killer
/plugin install m-dash-killer@compota334-plugins

## Requirements

Claude Code with plugin support. Python 3 on PATH. No external dependencies.

## Source

https://github.com/compota334/Em-Dash-Killer
